summary: Carded from Fabio's ask: one supplied image in, a character sheet out, with the front full body HEADLESS. Not new on the board but never a card - it was candidate workflow 4 in MPI-348 s8, whose own working mode says surfaced ideas get their own card. Carries the Higgsfield HELL GRIND sheet spec (3 panels, headless front body, large 3/4 portrait, boring flat grey with no grain baked in, mandatory pupil catch-light, pick believable over beautiful) and flags that it CONFLICTS with Fabio's own best-performing layout from past tests (side + front profile + full body) - settle at the bench. Names the real risk: their sheets came from a PROMPT in a hosted creative model, ours must hold identity onto a back view from one photo, and MPI-348 s7 already records Qwen-Edit as weak on single-image instruction edits. Headless panel specced as a SAM3 mask + empty-prompt klein inpaint, not a prompt, which also honours their never-run-an-image-through-a-model-twice rule. Id claimed with exclusive mkdir.

Re-scoped by Fabio. The MPI-348 s8.4 layout (side + front profile + full body) is a LORA-TRAINING sheet - a different consumer - so the two layouts are NOT a conflict to settle; layout becomes a flow option keyed to purpose, and this card owns the VIDEO-REFERENCE layout only. Input is now TWO paths: attributes-only (what the character is, wardrobe, scars, age, hair colour, eye colour) restructured into the sheet prompt, and a reference photo. The attributes path is the LOW-RISK one and ships first - it is exactly what Higgsfield did (prompt to sheet in a hosted model) and has no identity-projection problem; the photo path keeps the unproven back-view step. Added: with structured fields a slot template needs no LLM, so Cubric Prompt earns its place only on free prose or per-model shaping. Recorded that their 'never write an age' rule does NOT transfer - that is a hosted content filter and Vision runs local models.

Two corrections from Fabio. (1) The LoRA-training sheet is OUT OF SCOPE, not a layout option - it is ~20 images and a whole different beast, addressed when that flow is addressed; MPI-504 owns the video-reference 3-panel sheet only. (2) The flow needs TWO MODELS, chosen per path at the bench - an EDIT model for the reference path, and for the attributes path whichever t2i model best obeys a prompt asking it to display the character in that layout. That second question is LAYOUT COMPLIANCE, not aesthetics, and has no answer on the board. Multiple models in one flow is the point of flows.
